clue.text: Date when surveillance operation doesn't start

indicators.note: the operation's word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a stakeout is police surveillance of a place

explanation.surface: Police wait to spring a date, but the stakeout never begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link. Without its first letter, STAKEOUT leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out is to escort them on a romantic outing, which is what dating them means; a takeout is also a bridge bid.

clue.text: Score that's close, We and They showing nothing in it

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

parts.note: read as 'that has': the word that, whose close is wanted
N stands for 'and', as in rock 'n' roll

indicators.note: the word has its inside emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A tight bridge rubber, the We and They columns of the scorepad still blank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is read as 'that has': the close of THAT is T. WE comes as written, 'n' is 'and', and THEY emptied is TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a group of twenty, the number of the answer.

clue.text: Porridge shock, as had bears

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so these words carry the answer within them

explanation.surface: The bears of the Goldilocks story are shocked at their porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Kasha is an Eastern European porridge made from buckwheat or other grain.

clue.text: Going after tricks, to do with bridge?

parts.note: on means about or concerning
bridge is the game in this card-themed puzzle

explanation.surface: Seeking tricks, about bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, tricks are the rounds a player wins; here they are clients picked up by a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the game is British slang for working as a prostitute, soliciting for paying clients.

clue.text: Sharp finesse leading with fourth in suit

indicators.note: the single letter goes ahead of the skill word
the fourth letter of the word suit

parts.note: art is skill or finesse

explanation.surface: A sharp bridge finesse, played leading from the fourth card of the suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart describes a sour, acidic taste, sharp on the tongue.

clue.text: Uniform black boards benefit duplicate

indicators.note: to board is to get on or in, so these letters climb inside the benefit word

parts.note: the dole is British state unemployment benefit
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
B is the abbreviation for black (as on pencils)

explanation.surface: A uniformed black-clad figure sits on a benefits board that approves a duplicate claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Double as a verb means to copy or make twice, the same as duplicate; it is also a bridge call.

clue.text: Slighted, 8th Earl Spencer was furious

parts.note: John Spencer, 8th Earl Spencer, was Princess Diana's father: Di's pa
raged means was furious

explanation.surface: A snubbed aristocrat flies into a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparaged means belittled or spoken of with contempt, as one who was snubbed.

clue.text: Article lost by dirty man you're in a relationship with

definitions.text: man you're in a relationship with

indicators.note: the dirty word gives up the article

parts.note: unclean means dirty
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grubby boyfriend loses an item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a male relative, your parent's brother.

clue.text: Pay attention, Edna and learn to shuffle

indicators.note: shuffling mixes the letters like cards in a pack

explanation.surface: A teacher tells Edna to listen and learn how to shuffle cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is an idiom for listening carefully.

clue.text: Betty regularly keeps card up sleeve

indicators.note: in a down entry, the card word goes up top, above the kept letters

parts.note: a jack is a court card

indicators.note: the name keeps only its letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Betty, a card cheat, often has a card up her sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly keeps' takes every other letter of BETTY, giving ET; 'up' sets JACK above it in the down light, rather than reversing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket is the paper cover of a record or book, also called its sleeve.

clue.text: See smarty pants in comfortable contract

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are judged poor and rearranged

explanation.surface: A smart-alec gets a cushy deal in the small print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smarty pants' reads as one insult, but 'pants' (British slang for bad, rubbish) is the anagram signal for SEE and SMARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy terms are generous instalment arrangements in a purchase agreement, a lenient bargain.

clue.text: Trick starts to go awry — one is beaten

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick

indicators.note: the beginnings of the next two words are taken, one letter each

explanation.surface: A card trick begins to go wrong and its performer gets thrashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A conga is a tall Latin American drum, an instrument struck with the hands.

clue.text: Playing card expert on vacation run to ground

indicators.note: playing the letters of card around changes their order
a vacated word has its inside emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A card sharp away on holiday is finally hunted down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties EXPERT to ET; 'Playing' then shuffles CARD with ET.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something to ground is to find it after a search, which is to have tracked or located it.

clue.text: Fellow with excellent cards presents mask

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for Fellow, as in FRS
ace means first-rate
a pack is a full set of playing cards

explanation.surface: A man holding a strong hand puts on a poker face.
explanation.definitionFit: A face pack is a cosmetic paste spread over the face like a beauty mask.

clue.text: Biblical characters carrying powerful scent among possessions

indicators.note: the belongings word holds the smell inside it

parts.note: things means belongings
a reek is a strong smell

explanation.surface: Bible figures smell strongly of the goods they bring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magi brought frankincense and myrrh, hence the scent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Three Kings are the Magi of the Nativity story, gift-bearing wise men in the Gospel.

clue.text: Novel English combat sport

parts.note: MMA is mixed martial arts, a cage-fighting sport

explanation.surface: A new kind of English fighting sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the noun: a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is the Jane Austen book about a matchmaking heroine.

clue.text: Like bloody tissue, rank one in bog

indicators.note: the rank and one go inside the bog word

parts.note: a marsh is a bog
a row is a rank or line
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bloodied soldier from the ranks is lying in a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrowish means resembling bone marrow, the soft blood-making core within bones.

clue.text: Card table that's not large adjusted in a tick

parts.note: a heart is a card of that suit

indicators.note: the remaining letters are altered into a new order
the table word is said to be without the large letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothes

explanation.surface: A card table is shrunk and rearranged in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not large' drops L from TABLE to leave TABE, which 'adjusted' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is British for a moment, and a heartbeat is likewise a very brief instant.

clue.text: Child reformed Israel's system for the 20

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the name's letters are formed anew in a different order

parts.note: the name's letters; the 's only joins it to the next word

explanation.surface: A child reshapes the Israeli system.
explanation.definitionFit: A totaliser, or tote, is the pool betting system that pays out to punters at the racecourse.

clue.text: Endure each cut except the last

parts.note: per means each, as in 'a pound per head'

indicators.note: the cut word is taken without its final letter

parts.note: severed means cut off

explanation.surface: Put up with every snip but the final one.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, to hold out or last.

clue.text: Jerry bid second, giving reasons

parts.note: jerry is British slang for a chamber pot, as is po
1NT, one no-trump, is a bridge bid; read 1 as I

explanation.surface: A bridge player called Jerry bids next, explaining himself.
explanation.walkthrough: A jerry or po is a chamber pot, kept under the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Points are arguments or reasons put forward in a discussion.

clue.text: 28 24's; deck full of them?

parts.note: the answer to 28 across is THANKS, and TA is British informal for thanks
the answer to 24 down is QUEEN; R (Regina) is Queen, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that asks what a card deck is packed with.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is casual British for thank you; R is short for Regina, the Latin for queen. 'deck' means a ship's deck, not cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tars are sailors, who crowd the deck of a ship.

clue.text: Trump player

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to outdo, as a verb
second meaning: one who bets, a punter

explanation.walkthrough: A trump at cards and a card player both look like nouns; the first is the verb meaning to surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To better something is to improve on it, and a better is also a gambler placing wagers.

clue.text: Strong club opening for Lightner and Eisenhower

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

indicators.note: the opening letter of the bridge player's name

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A strong club opening bid, played by bridge expert Lightner partnering Eisenhower.
explanation.walkthrough: Theodore Lightner was a US bridge expert; Eisenhower was also a keen bridge player. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iron-like has the hardness and toughness of the metal, so it is sturdy.

clue.text: Card learner turned over gave the game away

indicators.note: turning a down entry over reads its letters from the bottom

parts.note: a card is a short written message, a note
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A beginner turns a card face up and gives away the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is an idiom for revealing a secret.

clue.text: Gang, how clever you are cracking this!

indicators.note: to crack is to break into, so the measure of cleverness gets inside

parts.note: this is a clue, the very thing being solved
IQ is a measure of intelligence

explanation.surface: A self-congratulating pat on the back for solving this clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is a small exclusive group of people, a set or circle.

clue.text: Name for R in rummy?

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: rummy is old British slang for strange or queer
the letter itself

explanation.surface: A card player asks what the R on a rummy card stands for.
explanation.walkthrough: R in rummy is Rex or Regina; the queen is also a card in the game of rummy.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina, abbreviated R, is the Latin word for a reigning queen, the female monarch.

clue.text: Deal hands face up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run upwards, reversed

parts.note: paws is informal for hands

explanation.surface: A card dealer turns hands face up.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to trade or exchange, to make a deal.

clue.text: Another card please, from spades in dummy

indicators.note: the spades letter goes inside the dummy word

parts.note: a twit is a fool, a dummy
S is the abbreviation for spades in card notation

explanation.surface: A player calls for another card while holding spades as dummy at bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' links; S sits inside TWIT. In pontoon (Britain's name for blackjack) you say 'twist' to be dealt another card.
explanation.definitionFit: Twist is the pontoon call asking the dealer for one more card face up.

clue.text: Bridge players recycled these articles

definitions.note: the sheet holds articles, so the plural stands for the paper that prints them

parts.note: the four players at bridge are named North, East, West and South

indicators.note: recycling turns the letters into something new

explanation.surface: The bridge four reuse old newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A news sheet is a simple single-page newspaper, made up of printed reports or stories.

clue.text: Tesla coils that'll do nicely

parts.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density
hanks are coils of yarn or rope

explanation.surface: Tesla coils, admired for working well.
explanation.definitionFit: 'That'll do nicely' is a grateful acknowledgement, the same appreciation as saying thank you.

clue.text: Taken aback by split, blame the player opposite

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
a rap is a reprimand or the blame, as in 'take the rap'

explanation.surface: Shocked by a break-up, a bridge player blames the person across the table.
explanation.definitionFit: At bridge your partner sits across from you, the teammate seated directly facing you.
